$y=x^2+2$, $P(x\,;\,x^2+2)$, $B(0\,;\,3)$

$\mathrm{PB}^2=(x-0)^2+(x^2+2-3)^2=x^2+x^4-2x^2+1=x^4-x^2+1$

$\mathrm{PB}$ will be a minimum if $\mathrm{PB}^2$ is a minimum.

$\dfrac{d}{dx}(\mathrm{PB}^2)=4x^3-2x$

$4x^3-2x=0$

$x(2x^2-1)=0$

$x=0$ or $x^2=\dfrac{1}{2}$

$x=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\mathrm{PB}^2=\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^4-\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+1=\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}+1=\dfrac{3}{4}$

$\mathrm{PB}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=0,87$

alternatives.label: OR
alternatives.working_md:
Gradient of the tangent to the curve $=2x$.

Gradient of the line joining $B$ and the curve $=\dfrac{x^2+2-3}{x-0}=\dfrac{x^2-1}{x}$.

The shortest distance is where the tangent is perpendicular to $BP$:

$\dfrac{x^2-1}{x}=-\dfrac{1}{2x}$

$2x(x^2-1)=-x$

$2x^3-2x=0$

$x(2x^2-1)=0$

$x=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\mathrm{PB}^2=\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^4-\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+1=\dfrac{3}{4}$

$\mathrm{PB}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=0,87$

alternatives.label: OR
alternatives.working_md:
$P(k\,;\,k^2+2)$ and $B(0\,;\,3)$.

$BP$ is perpendicular to the tangent to $y=x^2+2$ at $P$.

$m_{\text{tangent at }P}=2k$, $m_{BP}=-\dfrac{1}{2k}$

Equation of $BP$: $y=\left(-\dfrac{1}{2k}\right)x+3$

$y_P=\left(-\dfrac{1}{2k}\right)(k)+3=2,5$

$\Rightarrow k^2+2=2,5$, so $k=\sqrt{0,5}$ and $P(\sqrt{0,5}\,;\,2,5)$

$\mathrm{BP}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{0,5}-0)^2+(2,5-3)^2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{4}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=0,87$

parts.answer_md: Codes of two letters and five digits
parts.working_md:
Number of digits used, with letters $5\times 5$:

$1$ digit: $5\times 5\times 10=250$

$2$ digits: $5\times 5\times 10\times 9=2\,250$

$3$ digits: $5\times 5\times 10\times 9\times 8=18\,000$

$4$ digits: $5\times 5\times 10\times 9\times 8\times 7=126\,000$

$5$ digits: $5\times 5\times 10\times 9\times 8\times 7\times 6=756\,000$

Codes of two letters and five digits will ensure unique numbers for $700\,000$ clients.
